experiment.name: Linkage audit: which dogs appear in more than one file (DS02-DS07, S-CB050, S-CB517)
experiment.description: Which dogs are shared between the programme's files, and can a file without outcomes (DS07) be joined to one with death, age and sex? Descriptive: value matches within rounding where files share variables, chance-calibrated signalment matching where they do not.

parameters.tolerance: max(0.011, 0.5%) for two-decimal counts; Hct 0.005, retic 0.05

sections.heading: Question
paragraphs: Which dogs appear in more than one of the programme's files? Files that share dogs are not independent evidence, and a link to a file with death, age and sex could give a label to a file that lacks one (DS07).

sections.heading: What was done
paragraphs: Raw files only, standard-library Python. (1) DS04 haematology rows were joined to case numbers by the row order of the five Stats Tables sheets and checked against S-CB050 by WBC, segmented and band neutrophils within rounding, and by icterus wording against bilirubin. (2) Every DS04 row was searched in all 161 S-CB050 rows. (3) DS03 natural and control dogs were compared with S-CB050 on age, weight and sex, with DS05 (Eastern Cape, 2021) as a chance baseline; two checks were added after the first run: study-number order and a DS03-DS04 value check on haematocrit and reticulocytes. (4) DS06 names were mapped to DS02 dogs by sampling pattern and by marker-gene kinetics, with a positive control. (5) DS07 numbers were compared with DS04 numbers and with the CB112 group summaries.

sections.heading: Result
paragraphs: 10 links are confirmed by values, 11 are probable and 126 unverified (out/linkage.csv). DS04 cases 50, 54 and 59 are S-CB050 cases 126, 127 and 131 (three equal counts, equal signalment, all died); the row-order join that puts them there has a chance probability of 0.0014. The other seven fatal DS04 dogs match no S-CB050 row.

New: DS03's natural dogs are S-CB050 dogs. 77 of 78 cohort-1 dogs, 17 of 17 cohort-2 dogs and 12 of 13 controls have an age-weight-sex twin in the matching S-CB050 block, 59.3, 118.7 and 253.8 times the rate against DS05; every unique pair keeps the study-number order (Kendall tau 1.0 in all three blocks), and DS03 BLSC29 has the haematocrit (0.07) and reticulocyte % of DS04 case 54 = S-CB050 127.

DS07: 6 of the 7 DS04 numbers below 98 are DS07 'complicated' (expected about 1.01, p = 2.0e-05 over 1-97), so the numbering is probably shared. But DS04 case 20 is 144 months old (CB112 range 6-120) and case 88 was dead on arrival yet is DS07 'uncomplicated'. DS07 death cannot be taken from DS04 yet.
DS06: high_3 = DS02 dog 6 by sampling pattern. The marker-gene check did not recover that link (best assignment: high_1=dog 4; high_2=dog 6; high_3=dog 5), so the other DS06 names stay unverified.

sections.heading: What this does not show
paragraphs: Age, weight and sex identify a dog weakly; the DS03-S-CB050 dog-level pairs stay unverified even though the file-level overlap is clear. No link was made through DS07, which has no clinical values. Absence of a match does not prove different dogs: S-CB050 may have excluded dogs that another file kept. The independent_source changes are a proposal; /core/datasets.jsonl was not edited. 'Died' in the Onderstepoort files includes euthanasia for poor prognosis.
